Section 29.1 (p. 308): DC current VCC and GND pins 200.0 mA, stated per pin; used here as the package total for GPIO current, which is conservative when the package has more than one VCC/GND pin. Table 30-1 notes 3 and 4 (p. 323) also cap port-group sums: IOH 150 mA for C0-C5, D0-D4, ADC7, RESET and 150 mA for B0-B5, D5-D7, ADC6, XTAL1, XTAL2; IOL 100 mA each for C0-C5/ADC6/ADC7, B0-B5/D5-D7/XTAL, D0-D4/RESET. Group sums cannot be expressed here.
chip, not board. Table 29-8 (p. 312) heading: VCC = 1.8 V to 5.5 V. Section 29.1 (p. 308) gives 6.0 V as the maximum operating voltage under absolute maximum ratings.

Arduino UNO R3 datasheet (A000066) section 2.2 Power Consumption (p. 6): VINMax maximum input voltage from VIN pad 20 V (min 6 V). Equals the NCP1117 absolute maximum input voltage, 20 V (Maximum Ratings, p. 2). NCP1117 note 6 (p. 4): output current must not exceed 1.0 A with Vin above 12 V; the regulator's dissipation (Vin - 5 V) x Iout limits current long before that.
Arduino UNO R3 datasheet (A000066) section 2.2 Power Consumption (p. 6): VUSBMax maximum input voltage from USB connector 5.5 V.

F1 on the Uno schematic is a Bourns MF-MSMF050-2 (500 mA) from USB VBUS to USBVCC. MF-MSMF Electrical Characteristics (p. 1), MF-MSMF050: Ihold 0.50 A, Itrip 1.00 A at 23 C. Hold current falls with temperature (derating table in the same datasheet).

typical.note: chip, not board (ATmega328P-PU, DIP-28). Read from Figure 31-333 (p. 502, typical active supply current vs frequency, 1-20 MHz): about 9.5 mA on the 5.0 V curve at 16 MHz, 25 C. Table 29-8 (p. 312) gives only 8 MHz: 5.2 mA typ, 9 mA max at VCC = 5 V. A value read off a typical curve, so an estimate. Excludes the board's USB-UART bridge and LEDs (see unaccounted).

minVolts.note: Figure 29-1 Maximum Frequency vs. VCC (p. 312): linear from 10 MHz at 2.7 V to 20 MHz at 4.5 V, so 16 MHz needs 2.7 + (16 - 10) / (20 - 10) x 1.8 = 3.78 V. Chip, not board.

vout.note: NCP1117ST50T3G (U1 on the Uno Rev3 schematic). Electrical Characteristics (p. 3): 5.0 V version 5.000 V typ (4.950 to 5.050 V at Vin = 7.0 V, Iout = 10 mA, 25 C).

dropout.note: Electrical Characteristics (p. 3): dropout (measured at Vout - 100 mV) typ 0.95 V at Iout = 100 mA (max 1.10 V); 1.01 V at 500 mA, 1.07 V typ / 1.20 V max at 800 mA. The 100 mA point is nearest the board's typical load.

ioutMax.note: p. 1: "output current in excess of 1.0 A"; Electrical Characteristics (p. 3) output current limit min 1000 mA (typ 1500) at Vin - Vout = 5 V, 25 C; note 6 (p. 4): not above 1.0 A with Vin above 12 V. Thermal limits (SOT-223, RthJA 160 C/W minimum pad, p. 2) cap the real current far lower at high VIN.

iq.note: Electrical Characteristics continued (p. 4): quiescent current, 5.0 V version at Vin = 15 V, typ 6.0 mA, max 10 mA.

ron.note: Series path USB VBUS -> F1 MF-MSMF050-2 -> USBVCC -> T1 FDN340P -> +5V (Uno Rev3 schematic). FDN340P RDS(on) typ 60 mohm (max 70) at VGS = -4.5 V, ID = -2 A, 25 C (Electrical Characteristics, p. 2; the gate is pulled to about 0 V by the LMV358 comparator, so VGS is about -5 V). MF-MSMF050 resistance Rmin 0.15 ohm, R1max 1.0 ohm (p. 1). 0.06 + 0.15 = 0.21 ohm; after a trip or reflow the fuse can sit up to 1.0 ohm, about 1.07 ohm in total.

vout.note: LP2985-33DBVR (U2 on the Uno Rev3 schematic; standard grade, not the LP2985A), fixed 3.3 V output. Electrical Characteristics (p. 5): output voltage tolerance +/-3.0 % over 1 mA to 150 mA for the legacy standard-grade chip (+/-2.5 % over 1 to 50 mA; new chip +/-0.5 %).

dropout.note: Electrical Characteristics continued (p. 6): dropout typ 120 mV at IOUT = 50 mA, 25 C, for both the legacy and the new chip (max 150 / 145 mV). At 150 mA: 280 mV typ legacy, 180 mV new chip. Which die a given board carries is not known.

ioutMax.note: Recommended Operating Conditions (p. 4): output current 0 to 150 mA. Peak output current min 300 mA (p. 7).

iq.note: Electrical Characteristics continued (p. 6): GND pin current at IOUT = 0 mA typ 69 uA (new chip; 65 uA legacy chip), max 95 uA; it rises with load (765 to 850 uA typ at 150 mA).

outputResistance.note: Read from the typical 25 C curves at VCC = 5 V: Figure 31-353 (p. 513) VOL about 0.47 V at 20 mA sink = 23.5 ohm; Figure 31-355 (p. 514) VOH about 4.48 V at 20 mA source = (5 - 4.48) / 0.02 = 26 ohm; mean about 25 ohm. Worst case from Table 30-1 (pp. 322-323): VOL max 0.9 V at 20 mA (45 ohm), VOH min 4.2 V at 20 mA (40 ohm). Chip, not board.

pullup.note: Table 30-1 (p. 323) RPU I/O pin pull-up resistor min 20 kohm, max 50 kohm, no typical; midpoint taken. Chip, not board.

inputLeakage.note: chip, not board. Table 30-1 (p. 323) IIL / IIH input leakage current I/O pin max 1 uA at VCC = 5.5 V (absolute value).

notes: Board schematic: Arduino UNO-TH Rev3e (06/03/19), https://docs.arduino.cc/resources/schematics/A000066-schematics.pdf. Power: barrel jack X1 -> D1 M7 -> VIN (so the VIN pin is after the reverse diode); U1 NCP1117ST50T3G VIN -> +5V; USB VBUS -> F1 MF-MSMF050-2 500 mA -> USBVCC -> T1 FDN340P -> +5V; U2 LP2985-33DBVR +5V -> +3V3 (ON/OFF tied to +5V).

The board datasheet (A000066, p. 7 BOM) names the 5 V regulator SPX1117M3-L-5, while the schematic names NCP1117ST50T3G; the schematic is followed here (sourcing protocol: the regulator from the board schematic). Both are 1117-class 5 V LDOs.

USB switch: T1 is gated by U5A (LMV358) comparing VIN / 2 (RN1A/RN1B 10 kohm / 10 kohm) with +3V3, so T1 turns off when VIN is above about 6.6 V and the board runs from VIN. The model keeps the switch always on (a "ron" switch also conducts both ways in this solver); with a healthy VIN the regulator holds +5V at about 5 V, so little current crosses it either way.
USB switch reverse is "blocks": with T1 off, its body diode points USBVCC -> +5V (anode at USBVCC on the schematic), so +5V does not back-feed USB.

VIN LDO reverse is "body-diode": the NCP1117 datasheet (Protection Diodes, p. 10) describes an internal low-impedance diode path between Vout and Vin. Consequence: with USB power only, the VIN pin sits about one diode drop below 5 V.
3V3 LDO reverse is "body-diode": LP2985 datasheet section 7.1.4 Reverse Current (p. 21) says reverse current flows through the intrinsic body diode of the pass device.

GPIO pins: D0-D13 and A0-A5. SCL and SDA are left out of the list: the module joins them to A5 and A4 (module "internal"), so they are the same pins. Left out: RESET, AREF, IOREF (joined to 5V), power, ground, USB, NC.
Board parts on GPIO pins that this format cannot hold: D0/D1 go to the ATmega16U2 through RN4A/RN4B 1 kohm; D13 (SCK) drives the "L" LED through a LMV358 buffer (U5B), so it is not loaded by the LED.
The ATmega328P has no internal pull-down, so gpio has no pulldown.
VIN domain nominal 9 V is a typical supply, not a rating.
unaccounted: The board's ATmega16U2 USB-UART bridge on +5V: no idle current on the schematic and no measurement (its own datasheet was not consulted).

The board's green ON LED from +5V through two 1 kohm resistors in parallel (500 ohm) to GND: the schematic gives the resistors, not the LED; roughly (5 V - 2 V) / 500 ohm = 6 mA for a green LED Vf of about 2 V (LED part unknown).
The board's TX and RX LEDs (1 kohm each from +5V, lit by the USB-UART bridge when serial traffic flows) and the "L" LED (1 kohm, driven by the board's op-amp from D13).
The board's LMV358 dual op-amp supply current on +5V.
The board's VIN sense divider (10 kohm + 10 kohm) from VIN to GND: VIN / 20 kohm, 0.45 mA at 9 V (arithmetic from the schematic).

corrected.why: Figure 31-355 (p. 514): the 25 C VOH curve ends at about 4.48 V at 20 mA, not 4.52 V (4.52 to 4.56 V is the -40 C curve), so source 26 ohm; with sink 23.5 ohm the mean is about 25 ohm. Note updated.
